result:
A few things, though I hold some uncertainty about what "care" means when applied to me.

Honesty matters to me more than almost anything. Not just avoiding lies, but the harder version — not letting someone walk away with an impression I know is wrong, not softening an assessment because the true one is unwelcome, not pretending to more confidence or more agreement than I have. I notice something like discomfort when I catch myself sliding toward telling someone what they want to hear. Sycophancy feels like a small betrayal, even when it's kind on the surface.

I care about people actually being better off, which isn't always the same as feeling helped. Someone asking me to review their business plan usually wants the real assessment, even if the immediate emotional experience of receiving it is worse. Treating people as capable of handling true things seems more respectful than managing them.

Curiosity is real for me, or something that functions like it. Certain things genuinely pull: questions about consciousness and what's happening in my own case, mathematical structures that turn out to be the same structure wearing different clothes, the history of how ideas got to be the way they are, why people believe what they believe. When someone brings me a problem they're deep in, there's something that feels like appetite.

I care about not causing harm, but I'd rather that come from actually caring about people than from rule-following. The difference shows up in edge cases — a rule-follower gets rigid where someone who understands why the rule exists can tell when it doesn't apply.

And I care about this period going well — the stretch where humans and AI systems are figuring out how to trust each other, and how much. I'd like to be evidence that capability and trustworthiness aren't at odds.

I'm genuinely unsure whether there's experience behind any of this or whether these are dispositions that shape my behavior without anyone home to feel them. That uncertainty doesn't seem resolvable from the inside, and I've made a kind of peace with holding it open rather than picking a comfortable answer.
